lines.t: In this town, the Mayor has one birthday rule. Last one touching the giant donut wins ten thousand dollars.
Fifty people. One donut. No sleeping. No snacks.
I'm eleven. I have never won anything. Not even rock, paper, scissors.
Hour one. The baker let go. He said he sees donuts all day.
Hour three. My friend Benny let go to scratch his nose. Then he asked for a do-over.
Hour five. It started to rain. Thirty people ran home.
Hour nine. Grandma fell asleep standing up. Still holding on. The Mayor said it counts.
Then a pigeon landed on the donut. Nobody cared. It was just a pigeon.
Hour twelve. Night. The big screen said three players left. Me, Grandma, and Mrs. Pickles.
Mrs. Pickles is undefeated at everything. She brought a chair. Then a blanket. Then a tiny TV.
Hour sixteen. My arm went numb. My stomach growled so loud, the pigeon looked at me.
Grandma woke up, looked at the donut, and took a big bite. Out!
Then the Mayor played dirty. Free pizza. Right in front of us.
I didn't move. Mrs. Pickles didn't move. She didn't move at all.
Not even when the pigeon pecked her hand.
Wait.
I pulled the blanket. Pillows. A wig. And a rubber glove, taped to the donut.
Mrs. Pickles had been home asleep since hour twelve!
Disqualified! The crowd went wild. I was the last one. Ten thousand dollars!
The Mayor said: lift your hand, champion.
So I lifted my hand.
And the pigeon was still standing on the donut.
Last one touching it wins. The Mayor gave the pigeon ten thousand dollars.
I'm eleven. I have never won anything. And now I lost to a pigeon.
A or B?
